content:
jordan: Hey team — ACME (customer) opened a ticket: intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal-api.acme.internal since 06:00 UTC. Their app logs show 502s and lots of DNS failures. Any quick checks?

priya: can you paste a dig/nslookup from their app host (or a repro container)? also any recent infra changes (VPC moves, peering, resolver changes)? :thinking:

acme-engineer: pasted dig output below. Happens from various hosts in the VPC.

acme-engineer: ```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> internal-api.acme.internal +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 5667
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 0
acme-internal-host-1:/# cat /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 172.31.0.2
options timeout:1 attempts:5
```

sam: NXDOMAIN + Authority suggests resolver thinks no such name in the attached private hosted zone. Could be: 1) private hosted zone not associated to VPC 2) duplicate private zone in another account causing split-horizon 3) resolver rule/forwarder misroute.

jordan: They did a VPC migration yesterday (moved some services to a new VPC in same account). I asked for VPC id: vpc-0a1b2c3d. @lee can you confirm hosted zone associations for acme.internal and vpc-0a1b2c3d?

lee: checking... give me 2 mins.

lee: ```
$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name acme.internal
HostedZones:
  - Id: /hostedzone/Z111AAA111
    Name: acme.internal.
    CallerReference: ...
    Config: PrivateZone=true
    Account: 123456789012
  - Id: /hostedzone/Z222BBB222
    Name: acme.internal.
    CallerReference: ...
    Config: PrivateZone=true
    Account: 210987654321
```

lee: looks like there are two private hosted zones with the same domain across accounts. The VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d is only associated with Z222BBB222 (account 210987654321). The zone we expect (Z111AAA111 in ACME's account 123456789012) is NOT associated.

priya: aha. That explains intermittent success — if queries hit a resolver in the peered/forwarding path that goes to the expected zone it resolves, otherwise NXDOMAIN. Did ACME change resolver rules/forwarders or peering yesterday during migration?

acme-engineer: we did update a resolver rule to forward acme.internal to a central DNS account during migration. We rolled back but not sure associations were re-applied.

sam: remediation plan: 1) confirm which hosted zone contains the correct records (Z111AAA111 vs Z222BBB222) 2) associate the correct hosted zone with vpc-0a1b2c3d OR update resolver rules to prefer the correct zone 3) remove/rename duplicate hosted zone if it's stale OR set explicit resolver rules to avoid split-horizon.

lee: I inspected records — Z111AAA111 has the service A records. Z222BBB222 is an old staging zone with no matching records. I'll try to associate Z111AAA111 with vpc-0a1b2c3d, but cross-account associations require permission.

jordan: @lee please escalate to infra if you need cross-account assoc permissions. Also can we temporary add a conditional forwarder so ACME queries go to the correct resolver?

lee: opened infra ticket: INF-4987 (cross-account zone association). In the meantime I added a stub resolver rule on the VPC to forward acme.internal to the resolver in acct 123456789012 (priority high).

support-bot: Ticket INF-4987 created and assigned to infra-team.

acme-engineer: after the temporary forwarder went live we see immediate improvement — dig returns A records now. We'll monitor for 15m. :thumbsup:

(15 minutes later)

acme-engineer: confirmed: all app instances now resolve internal-api.acme.internal and HTTP 200s returned. Looks stable.

jordan: great. Next steps: infra to finalize cross-account association or consolidate hosted zones to avoid future split-horizon. Also update runbook with checklist for VPC migrations (check hosted zone associations / resolver rules).

lee: will follow up in INF-4987 with permanent assoc and postmortem notes.

priya: please add the dig outputs and the temporary fix commands to the support ticket so CS can close with the customer.

jordan: ACME confirmed in ticket and on call. Closing from support side once infra confirms permanent assoc. Thanks everyone. :eyes:
